title: Minimum Operations to Write the Letter Y on a Grid
summary: Given an n x n grid where n is odd, each cell contains 0, 1, or 2.
statement: Given an n x n grid where n is odd, each cell contains 0, 1, or 2. The task is to determine the minimum operations needed to make the grid represent the letter Y. The letter Y is formed if the cells in the Y shape are uniform, the cells outside the Y are uniform, and the values within and outside the Y are different. An operation changes a cell's value to 0, 1, or 2.
constraints: grid is an odd-size square matrix of values zero, one, and two.
The Y consists of both upper diagonals through the center and the center column from the center downward.
All Y cells need one value and all other cells a different value; return the minimum cell changes.
hints: Only the frequency of each value inside and outside the fixed Y shape matters.
Classify every cell, count its value in one of two groups, and try the six distinct value assignments.
For Y value a and outside value b≠a, changes=Ysize-countY[a]+outsideSize-countOutside[b].
For a fixed assignment, every disagreeing cell must change and every agreeing cell can remain; checking all assignments finds the global minimum.
editorial: For a fixed assignment, every disagreeing cell must change and every agreeing cell can remain; checking all assignments finds the global minimum.

tests.explanation: Choosing one for the Y and zero outside requires three changes.
Choosing one for the Y and zero outside changes the center and two stem cells, for three operations.
